disposition_reasoning: The Frozen Contract's data_lineage explicitly specifies 'Binance public USD-M Futures aggTrades archive' as the historical/future price source -- i.e. Binance's own aggregated-trade data product, not a raw individual-trade feed.

All 8 required days' aggregate_trade_id (the row-level identifier for published aggTrade records) are fully continuous, with zero gaps at any of the 7 cross-day boundaries -- no archive-level aggTrade row is missing.

Binance's own Futures API documentation states aggTrades aggregates and returns market trades only; insurance-fund and ADL trades are excluded from aggTrades by design. This means a gap in the underlying first_trade_id/last_trade_id range does not, by itself, establish that archive data was lost -- though it likewise does not prove the observed 107,349 gaps ARE fully accounted for by this mechanism either.

The binance-public-data GitHub repository has a prior issue (#378) showing the same pattern observed here -- aggregate_trade_id continuous, small first/last_trade_id gaps -- without official resolution, establishing this pattern as a known (if unexplained) characteristic of Binance's own aggTrades data, not unique to this project's copy.

A separate, categorically different type of report exists on the same repository (issue #350) describing actual aggTrades missing-entries incidents, which manifest as gaps in agg_trade_id itself (archive-row-level loss). This project's 8-day audit shows no such signal.

The Frozen Discovery Contract's eligibility block does not pre-register 'first_trade_id/last_trade_id fully contiguous' as a criterion. Introducing it now as a hard blocking gate after the fact would be adding a new post-hoc acceptance criterion not present in the frozen pre-registration, which conflicts with the project's own preregistration/frozen-semantics discipline.
